tagline: Over the Wasatch Plateau and down two canyons of coal country.
intro: From Fairview, SR-31 follows Cottonwood Creek up Fairview Canyon and tops out on the Wasatch Plateau at about 8,800 feet, where the loop splits. The south branch climbs past 9,600 feet by Huntington and Cleveland reservoirs and follows Huntington Creek down its canyon to the town of Huntington. The north branch runs along Electric Lake and over into Eccles Canyon, down to Scofield and its reservoir and on toward Colton.
This is coal country, and still working. Skyline Mine operates along the route, and Electric Lake keeps enough water in store to cool a power plant through a four-year drought.

moments.title: Huntington Reservoir
moments.text: Crews rebuilding the dam here in 1988 turned up the nearly complete skeleton of a Columbian mammoth some 9,500 years old. It is on display now at the museum in Price.

moments.title: Electric Lake
moments.text: A 1974 reservoir high on the east slope of the plateau, held for irrigation and power plant cooling. The highways along its shores are maintained year-round.

moments.title: Winter Quarters
moments.text: Fourteen miners caught for months by snow in the winter of 1877 gave the camp its name. On May 1, 1900, an explosion in the Number Four mine killed 200 men.
